Im not happy. I didnt pay any money for it, thankfully, but from what Ive played so far its not very well done. The thing I was most looking forward to was base-building and defending, which completely sucks in my opinion. Walls snap at strange places, the unevenness of the ground makes things float in super unrealistic manners, whatever I built it never actually looked like something. The process of gathering resources is even worse: you just click on an object (in some cases an entire house) and it vanishes into thin air, while your resource counters go up... There is absolutely no way to make this any more boring.

Another thing Id like to mention is the first quest I did, which I think is the start of the minutemen questline (minor spoilers I guess but nothing major that will be lost). You basically have to unlock one simple door to get a power core to get a suit of power armor aka endgame armor that I thought in most games you tend to get at the end of a game instead of after 30 minutes of playing. Now the only way to make this even worse is what comes next:

You now have pretty much the strongest armor in the game (plus a minigun, which is arguably one of the most lategame weapons as well), and guess what! You now have to fight the stronges goddamn enemy in the game. All within 30 minutes of playing. God dammit.

I say wait for a) mods to be released to at the very least fix this buggy mess and b) wait for the price to go down to maybe 10 or 15 bucks. At that point it might be worth it but only time will tell...

It is a better overall world then FO3, and that includes characters. The no speech checks is tough because without the alt dialogue conditions, it doesn't feel like a Fallout game personally, but understand that they wanted it more cinematic. There are also a few different choices like the power armor early, or terminals not locking up permanently that make it more "forgiving".

However, it still has a lot of what people like in FO3 (and to a much lesser extent NV). Weather in the Wasteland finally feels properly done. Just walking along feels like a good mix of FO3 and NV, it still has a lot of urban, and wild areas, and I like exploring. While you get the power armor far too early, jumping off a bridge or building wearing the armor feels good. So is painting your armor in flames, and having a few on display. Companions are better then FO3, don't know how they shape up compared to NV yet. The Brotherhood is not retconned into idiots. I have always been a hoarder in Fallout, so I like the building systems. As well, I don't mind the building settlements, feel much more attached to my home base then in FO3 or NV.

This is so far the best review I have seen on the game, as it matches up right with my own. Particularly "if you play the game like Diablo or Borderlands, you’ll have considerably more fun than you would have otherwise. As much as it pains me to admit it, Fallout 4 is actually quite enjoyable if you just want a quick RPG-lite FPS hybrid that is heavy on the gunplay and generous about its ammo and equipment. Like oldschool action RPGs, Fallout 4 is more about hoarding rare loot and killing things than telling a story or allowing for player choice."

I would rate NV 10/10 with mods, FO3 and FO4 roughly 7-8/10, all for different reasons. I think in 4-12 months time, different mods will fix different aspects of FO4. And what is funny is that the game has been out a short time, and a good chunk of people are quick on the "get Obsidian back to do a proper sequel" (even though that is even more unlikely then any other demands about the games based on their fall out). I love the world, and I don't mind the settlement building, so I am much more inclined to give FO4 a larger pass then others.
